newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends softer; uptrend seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends softer; uptrend seen.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate closed slightly lower on Wednesday amid loose liquidity in the banking system but dealers said they expected the rate to rebound toward 5.00 percent due to expected month-end liquidity demand.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 4.906 percent against Tuesday's 4.967 close, with the 30-day commercial paper stable at 4.80-4.85 against 4.85-4.90.

Dealers said they expected liquidity to tighten gradually because the central bank issued T$5 billion in three-month negotiable certificates of deposit at a single yield of 5.10 percent on Wednesday afternoon.
The government bond market reported no trade in the afternoon.
Bond yields were expected to rise on Thursday after the central bank said it had no intention to further loosen its monetary policy, traders said.
